chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), if you set it aside while you are seeking a place for it or waiting for a man (to receive it), there is no objection to it.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms-tax given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.عَزَلْتَهَا: You set it aside / separated it
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to hold Zakat al-Fitr while looking for the recipient?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic status of *Ihtibat* (setting aside) Zakat al-Fitr during the search for a recipient, affirming its permissibility even if the holder waits for a specific person. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the purity of the obligation itself, distinguishing between the act of separation and the final distribution. This ruling alleviates anxiety for donors, ensuring that the temporary holding period does not nullify the spiritual merit of the charity.
